notes:
I couldn't research this, so I have no commentary notes to give you.

My first try ran ten searches at once and went over the search tool's usage limit before any results came back. When I retried with a single search, the tool said I had no tool calls left for this turn. So I didn't open any of the approved sites, and I have no URLs to cite.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, and I haven't read any. Notes on 2 Timothy 3 written from my own memory, with no sources behind them, would break that, so I've left them out.

**What I'd do on the next attempt** (searches spread out so they don't hit the limit again):

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:**
   - Enduring Word on 2 Timothy 3
   - Bible Hub's pages for each verse (Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary)
   - Precept Austin's commentary on 2 Timothy 3
   - StudyLight as a backup
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ**, mainly on vv. 15–17 (what "God-breathed" means, Scripture's sufficiency and inerrancy). I'd also look at vv. 1–5 ("last days") and v. 12 (persecution):
   - Methodist: Wesley's Notes on wesley.nnu.edu
   - Reformed: Ligonier and The Gospel Coalition
   - Baptist: Grace to You (gty.org) and Desiring God
   - Lutheran: LCMS and 1517
   - Pentecostal: Sam Storms and the Assemblies of God site (ag.org)
3. **Other views:**
   - Catholic and Orthodox: catholic.com and New Advent on v. 16 and *sola scriptura*
   - Modern scholarship: NET Bible notes on *theopneustos* ("God-breathed") and Jannes and Jambres (v. 8), and Bible Odyssey on who wrote the Pastoral Letters
   - Prosperity teaching: Got Questions or similar pages, for how it fits with v. 12 ("all who desire to live godly lives… will be persecuted")

If you ask me again in a new message, I'll start with Enduring Word and the Bible Hub commentaries and build the notes verse by verse.
